newsitem.title: USA: U.S. company to work on N. Korean plants.
newsitem.headline: U.S. company to work on N. Korean plants.

text.p: A North Carolina-based company has signed a contract to serve as technical support consultant to a light-water nuclear reactor project in North Korea, the U.S.-led consortium overseeing the project announced Tuesday.
The Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation (KEDO) and Duke E&S signed a contract on Oct. 25, KEDO said.

Duke E&S is a subsidiary of Duke Power Co., a nuclear utility company based in Charlotte, N.C., and was selected through a competitive bidding process, KEDO said. Duke has extensive international experience designing, building and operating nuclear plants, KEDO said.

The work of design, manufacture, procurement, construction and management of the reactor project will be carried out by KEDO's prime contractor, the Korea Electric Power Corp. of the Republic of Korea, KEDO said.
The role of Duke E&S is to assist KEDO in supervising the overall implementation of the light water reactor project, KEDO said.

KEDO, run by governments of the United States, South Korea and Japan under a 1994 nuclear agreement between Washington and Pyongyang, is the international consortium working with North Korea to build two light-water nuclear reactors.
Under the $4.5 billion deal, Washington promised Pyongyang two light-water reactors if the isolationist communist state froze and ultimately dismantled its existing nuclear programme.
Light-water reactors are less suitable for producing weapons-grade plutonium than the graphite-moderated reactors built by North Korea.
